1. Start with the inspection records.

completion:
Include details on the malfunction or failure of the brakes on the vehicle.
3. Note any unusual noises from the brakes like grinding or squealing.
4. Describe what occurred during the stop on the vehicle and how the brake pedal felt like.
5. Take care to note any other indication of brake failure like a sagging pedal.
6. Write any tests performed to identify the problem (such as latency).
7. Add measurements taken during the tests.
8. Ensure the documentations about failed tests are accurate, detailed and adequate to assist with repair.
9. Follow instructions listed in local regulations and industry standards for proper documentations.
10. When in doubt, add any additional relevant information despised by the inspector from visual inspection or other sources.
